case.question: Will Pope Leo XIV be TIME Person of the Year 2026?
case.operative_rule: Yes if TIME explicitly names Pope Leo XIV its 2026 Person of the Year (including qualifying multiple-person naming); special cover/feature/group clauses remain as frozen. If no announcement by 2027-06-30 23:59 ET, No.

facts.finding: TIME describes an annual editorial choice: the person(s) most affecting news and lives for good or ill and embodying the year. Its 2025 AI Architects selection was made by editors. The page describes the selection process, not a 2026 shortlist or poll-based decision.
TIME reports Leo's Jan 9 address to Vatican diplomats, criticism of diplomacy based on force, and remarks on Ukraine and Venezuela. This is current-year coverage, not a POY announcement.
Official text confirms the Jan 9 annual New Year address to the accredited diplomatic corps and discusses multilateralism, force, war, Ukraine, and Venezuela.

TIME's 2013 finalists list includes Pope Francis, but separately states TIME readers' poll selected Egypt's General al-Sisi. The poll is not presented as the editorial winner-selection mechanism. This page alone does not establish the final 2013 winner.

coverage_limits.2026_shortlist_or_announcement: No actual 2026 TIME winner/shortlist announcement surfaced in the bounded checks. TIME's tag endpoint returned HTTP 401 (logs/deep_review_20261017/346_time_vatican_1205/time_poy_tag.receipt.json); this is an access limitation, not evidence that no shortlist exists.
coverage_limits.reader_poll: 2013 TIME finalist page explicitly distinguishes reader poll from editorial title; no 2026 poll was used as winner evidence.
coverage_limits.prior_papal_winners: This pass captured TIME's 2013 finalists list, which includes Pope Francis, but did not capture an official winner page; no broader pope-winner-history claim is made.
coverage_limits.prior_sources: Existing work/0346_facts_1200.json links hashed Vatican biography and TIME 2025 winner captures: May 8 2025 election/name; Dec 11 2025 Architects of AI.
